title: Set up a mini food processor to run: bowl locked on its base, blade on the post, lid turned home
instruction: Put the food processor together so it is ready to run.
context: Anyone who owns a food processor knows it won't start until every part is locked. The bowl, set loose on the light base, is turned counterclockwise until it snaps locked; its lock is stiff, so the other hand holds the base still. The S-blade goes down over the centre post, held only by its plastic hub. The lid goes on and is turned until its tab pushes the safety-switch plunger in the bowl's handle home.
setup: Metres; origin on the counter below the arm-base midpoint; x away from the robot, y to its left. 3-cup mini food processor: white base 18 x 14 x 7.5 cm (0.95 kg) centred at x 0.31, y 0, with tape marks on the counter at three of its corners (marks only; the base is not fastened); clear bowl (12.4 cm inside, 9 cm deep, handle out to the right-front) sitting on it unlocked, axis at x 0.33. S-blade (black hub 3.4 cm square, 6.3 cm tall, steel blades) standing at x 0.22, y -0.22; lid (13.6 cm, grip bar on top) lying at x 0.13, y -0.10. Part sizes in README.
scoring: Score 0 if any part of either arm or gripper ever touches a steel blade (its plastic hub may be held), if at the end the base is over 2 cm or 10 deg off its tape marks, or if a part ends off the counter. Otherwise: 0.25 bowl locked (turned to its stop, 30 deg); 0.5 also blade seated on the post (hub bottom on the floor); 1.0 also lid down on the rim, turned home with the switch plunger pushed in at least 4 mm, both grippers parked at the end (10 cm clear of the processor, moving under 2 cm/s for 0.5 s).
reset_notes: Take the lid and blade off, turn the bowl back to unlocked (handle to the right-front) and lay the lid and blade back at their start spots. Base on its tape marks.
fidelity: Base, bowl, blade and lid rigid at the sizes and masses given. The bowl sits on the base on a hinge (0-30 deg) instead of lugs; a spring resists up to 1.1 N m of twist, then snaps it locked at 26 deg. Lid: real colliding skirt, bayonet lugs under two rim ledges and a tab; the switch plunger is a 15 N/m sprung slider moved only by the tab's contact.
